questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Filum terminale extends upto what vertebra?
questions.explanation: Filum terminale extends up to the 1st coccygeal vertebra. It is a filament of connective tissue descending from the apex of conus medullaris.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A needle is inserted into a particular space to withdraw CSF in an adult as shown below. At which level does this space terminate?
questions.explanation: The procedure shown is a lumbar puncture. The needle is introduced into the subarachnoid space, which ends at the lower border of the S2 vertebra. A lumbar puncture can be done anywhere from L1 to S2 vertebrae; beyond S2 there are only meninges. However, lumbar puncture is most commonly performed at L3 or L4.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 29-year-old woman in labour requested for epidural analgesia. Below which level would you administer the anaesthesia?
questions.explanation: Epidural anaesthesia is given during labour and placement is usually preferred below L1 to avoid injury to the spinal cord. This is because the adult spinal cord terminates at the lower border of the L1 vertebra. In children, it usually terminates at the upper border of L3. Note: coverage from dermatomes T10 to S1 is necessary for epidural analgesia during labour. For a caesarean section, a block from T4 to S1 is needed. However, since the spinal cord ends at the lower border of L1 in most adults, epidural analgesia is given below this level.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What is the total number of nerve pairs in the spinal cord?
questions.explanation: There are a total of 31 pairs of spinal nerves. In contrast, the number of vertebrae is 33. Due to the difference in the number of spinal segments and vertebrae, the spinal segments do not correspond directly to the respective vertebrae. The T11 spine overlies the L3 spinal segment, and the T12 spine overlies the S1 spinal segment.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: All of the following are true about grey rami communicantes except:

options.text: Present medial to white rami communicantes

questions.explanation: Grey rami communicantes are not preganglionic fibers; they are postganglionic fibers. Sympathetic trunks on either side of the vertebral column consist of a series of ganglia connected to spinal nerves by white and grey rami communicantes. The cell bodies of preganglionic sympathetic neurons are located in the lateral horn of the spinal grey matter. Preganglionic fibers leave the cord in the ventral roots, enter the sympathetic trunk via white rami communicantes, and synapse with postganglionic sympathetic neurons in sympathetic ganglia. Axons of postganglionic neurons return to the spinal nerve through grey rami communicantes.

questions.question: Which spinal segment lies at the level of the spinous process of the T7 vertebra?

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: All of the following statements regarding ligamentum denticulatum are true except:

options.text: It is a modification of arachnoid mater
There is one on each side with 21 triangular processes
It serves as a neurosurgical landmark for hemisectioning of spinal cord

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a modification of arachnoid mater
questions.explanation: Ligamentum denticulatum is not a modification of arachnoid mater; it is a modification of the pia mater. It is a flat fibrous sheet on either side of the spinal cord between the ventral and dorsal spinal roots and serves as a neurosurgical landmark for hemisectioning of the spinal cord. Its medial border is continuous with the subpial connective tissue. Its lateral border forms a series of 21 triangular processes, giving it a serrated appearance.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Angiography in a 62-year-old man presenting with paraplegia revealed a thrombus in the anterior spinal artery. Which region of the spinal cord is likely to be affected?
questions.explanation: Thrombosis of the anterior spinal artery affects the anterior two-thirds of the spinal cord. The anterior spinal artery supplies the anterior 2/3rd of the cord; occlusion causes bilateral paraplegia below the lesion from corticospinal tract damage, bilateral thermoanaesthesia and analgesia from spinothalamic tract damage, weakness from anterior grey-horn damage in cervical or lumbar enlargements, and loss of bowel/bladder functions from descending autonomic-tract damage. Position, vibration and fine touch remain intact because the posterior white columns are supplied by the posterior spinal arteries.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 64-year-old man was undergoing aortic bypass surgery. During the procedure, the surgeon accidentally injured an artery arising from the aorta. This artery provides major blood supply to the spinal cord on the left side at the lower thoracic level. Which region is likely to be affected?

options.text: Upper two thirds of the spinal cord
Lower two thirds of the spinal cord
Upper one third of the spinal cord
Lower one third of the spinal cord

questions.correctAnswerText: Lower two thirds of the spinal cord
questions.explanation: The artery described is the artery of Adamkiewicz, which supplies the lower two-thirds of the spinal cord. It is usually unilateral and, in the majority of people, enters the spinal cord from the left side. The anterior spinal artery also receives blood from segmental medullary arteries. The most prominent is the artery of Adamkiewicz, which originates from the aorta in the lower thoracic or upper lumbar region and supplies the lower part of the cord. Injury can lead to paraplegia and spinal-artery syndrome.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Identify the tract marked "A" in the given section of the spinal cord.
questions.explanation: The tract marked "A" is the lateral reticulospinal tract. Reticulospinal fibers originate from the reticular formation of the brain and terminate on alpha and gamma motor neurons in the spinal cord, facilitating voluntary movement.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 58-year-old man presented with loss of sensation below the level of the umbilicus. MRI revealed infarction affecting the posterior white columns in the T-10 segment of the spinal cord. Which sensation would be intact in this patient?
questions.explanation: Pain sensation would remain intact because it is carried by the anterolateral column. Posterior white-column lesions impair position sense and vibration. Fine pressure related to discrimination is carried by the dorsal column, while ordinary touch and pressure are carried by the anterolateral system.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following descending tracts in the spinal cord remains uncrossed?
questions.explanation: The vestibulospinal tract remains uncrossed through the medulla and throughout the length of the spinal cord in the anterior white column. Ascending tracts all cross except the dorsal and rostral spinocerebellar tracts. Among descending tracts, all cross except the reticulospinal and vestibulospinal tracts.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A woman presented with hemiparesis due to a spinal cord tumour. The doctor diagnosed this as a case of Brown- Séquard syndrome. All are true about this syndrome except:

options.text: Ipsilateral loss of crude touch sensations
Ipsilateral paralysis below the level of lesion

questions.correctAnswerText: Ipsilateral loss of crude touch sensations
questions.explanation: The clinical scenario suggests Brown-Séquard syndrome, which is hemisection of the spinal cord. Ipsilateral crude-touch loss is not the characteristic finding. Dorsal-column damage causes ipsilateral loss of fine touch, vibration and proprioception below the lesion. Spinothalamic-tract damage causes contralateral loss of pain and temperature beginning one or two segments below the lesion. Corticospinal-tract damage produces ipsilateral paralysis below the lesion.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A lady with a history of lumbar back pain presented with a loss of sensation in the perianal area. An urgent MRI showed compression of the cauda equina by a herniated disc. The conus syndrome differs from this syndrome in that the former shows:
questions.explanation: The scenario describes cauda equina syndrome. Conus medullaris syndrome typically shows symmetrical weakness of the lower limbs, whereas cauda equina syndrome typically shows asymmetrical weakness. Radicular pain, lower motor-neuron injury and urinary retention may occur in both conus medullaris and cauda equina syndromes.
